blue.step0.what: A cell $(i,j)$ is the offset of the point $(x+i,d+j)$ from a base point $(x,d)$. We pack the shape $S$ of region type $0$ into $(x,d)$ with its neighbours $\pm1$.
blue.step1.what: For each prime $p\le B$ pick a class $(a,b)$ modulo $p$ that contains no neighbour of $S$ and set $x\equiv-a$, $d\equiv-b\pmod p$. The cells of $S$ in that class get region type $0$.
blue.step2.what: Every cell $(i,j)$ of $S$ outside these classes gets its own prime $q>B$ with $q\mid x+i$ and $q\mid d+j$.
blue.step3.what: The conditions on $d$ join into $d\equiv D\pmod{M_d}$, and $d$ is the first $D+tM_d$ with $d+j\ge1$ on every row.
blue.step4.what: The neighbours only need $\gcd(x+i,d+j)=1$. With $x\equiv X\pmod{M_x}$ from the conditions on $x$, the first $x=X+tM_x$ that passes at every neighbour is taken.
blue.step5.what: From $(x,d)$ alone: every cell of $S$ and of its neighbours gets its symbol $\left(\frac{x+i}{d+j}\right)$, and the region of a cell of $S$ must be exactly $S$.
